33. P.W. 30 is Shah Akil Uddin, O.C. In his deposition he stated that on 6.8.91 he was the officer-in-charge of Sarail Police Station and took over charge of the investigation of the case as I.O. on 11.8.91, visited the place of occurrence, examined the witnesses, recorded the statements under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure of 11 witnesses and after completion of the investigation submitted charge sheet. He further stated that accused Abdul Ali made a dying declaration. In his cross-examination he admitted that accused Kutubuddin was the sitting Chairman of Union Parishad at the time of occurrt. ace and admitted that a notice dated 14.7.1991 was served by him upon 7(seven) persons which is exhibit-A. He further admitted that accused Saidur was another Union Parishad member at the time of occurrence. He further admitted that during investigation he could not get any alamat or evidence of dacoity but found alamats of murder and therefore he submitted charge sheet under section 302 of the Penal Code. 

 34. This is all the evidences adduced by the prosecution. In this connection it will be profitable to refer to the confessional statement made by accused Abdul Ali exhibit-10 recorded under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. The relevant portion of the confessional statement of accused Abdul Ali is as under:- 

 37. The learned Advocate appearing for the condemned prisoner Kh. Golzar Hossain submitted that admittedly in the very night of the occurrence P.W. 25 Priadorshi Barua, the first I.O. of the case along with his farce went to Aropail Union Parishad Chairman Office where the dead body was kept and he stayed with the persons and all the witnesses of the inquest report there throughout the night including P.W.1. But at no point of time during the night any name of the accused was disclosed to P.W. 25 or to any other witnesses present and therefore the subsequent discloser of the names on the following morning after lapse of about 15 hours by P.W.1 naming 2 persons, namely, accused Abdul Ali and Abdul Awal is highly doubtful and should be taken as embellishment and should not be given any prudence. Refering to the statements of P.Ws. 7,8 and 9 who were the boat men the learned Advocate has submitted that if their statements are compared with the statements of P.W.1 it will appear that they contradicted each other on material particulars and therefore their evidences should be held as tainted evidence and cannot corroborate another piece of tainted evidence. Referring to the statements of P.W.18 Uttom Kumar Roy, P.W.20 Sebak Roy, P.W.21 Dr. Lakshmikanta Das the learned Advocate submitted that each of these witnesses made an attempt to implicate more persons falsely by saying that they recognized some of them although the so-called First Information Report Exhibit-1 was lodged 15 hours after the occurrence on the following morning and in presence of all of them which was read over to the informant and to the witnesses present. But the names of no other person other than the accused Abdul Ali and Awal were disclosed by the informant to P.W.25 and he has also drawn our attention referring to the statements of P.W. 23 Gopal Chandra Gop who in his cross-examination admitted as under: 

 41. We have already discussed that exhibit which was recorded at 7-30 on 6.8.91 is the first information report in this case being first in point of time and exhibit-1 is simply the statement of P.W. 1 recorded under section 161 Cr. P.C. In the statement before the police under section 161 as per exhibit-1 it appears that P.W. 1 did state that accused Abdul Awal gave a lathi blow on Paritosh Kunda where upon he fell into the water whereas while deposing before the Court as P.W.  he did not say who give the lathi blow on the person of Paritosh Kunda. It appears from the deposition of P.W.1 that he did not disclose the name of any accused to these who assembled there or to the I.O. P. W. 25 with whom he was admittedly there till 6-30 of the next morning. Thus non discloser of the name of any accused at or about the time of occurrence when good opportunity presented itself to him is enough to make his subsequent discloser of names doubtful inasmuch as no explanation has been given by the prosecution for such non-discloser of the names of the accused to the witnesses or to the I.O. It appears from his deposition that he and others sent one Solaiman Chowkider to the police with information of the occurrence but that Solaiman Chowkider has not been examined. Besides. P.W.25 in his deposition stated that he received the information through one Parimal Chanda Ghose who has also been withheld in this Court. Besides P.W.15 Md. A. Khaleque the subsequent Chairman of Union Parishad, stated that he and others informed the police station in respect of the dead body. No evidence is forthcoming as to what was the information sent by P.W.15 and what was the information given by Chowkider Solaiman and what was the information received by the informer. Withholding of the different information by prosecution make the prosecution case as to the first information to the police station shrouded in mystery. On scrutiny of deposition of the P.W.7 Abu Salek, the boat man it appears that he stated in his deposition that another boat man Ali Akbar assaulted the dacoits with the stick and stated that Saidur gave a lathi blow on Paritosh Kunda whereupon he fell into the water. Whereas he is contradicted on this point by P.W.8.and P.W. 9 inasmuch as P.W.9 does not say that he assaulted any dacoit and does not say Saidur gave the lathi blow on the dacoits although both are the boatman. Therefore either P.W. 7 is lying or P.W.9 is lying and such view of the matter it must be held that they were not present at the scene of the occurrence. Besides P.W.9 admitted that P.W.1 lodged the First Information Report at the police station and it was read over to him and others who were present there. But although in his deposition he implicated accused Abdul Ali, Razzaque, Sabur and A. Noor but none of them was named in exhibit-1 which was recorded in his presence and read over to the informant and to the witnesses informant P.W.9. This clearly shows and support the contention of the learned Advocate for the condemned prisoner that it is a clear case of embellishment. It is admitted position that the dead body was recovered with the help of two divers but none of them has been examined in this case. No explanation has been given for such withholding. This shows that the place of occurrence and the manner of occurrence is very much doubtful and a legitimate inference under section 114(g) of the Evidence Act can be drawn against the prosecution. 

 42. As to the manner of occurrence the learned Advocate further submits that the consistent case of the prosecution is that accused Abdul Ali gave a blow (ঘাই) by a pal which is pointed weapon whereupon he fell into the water but from the deposition of P.W.27 Dr. Abdul Gani Khondaker it does not appear that he found any punctured or penetrated wound on the dead body. This inconsistency of the ocular evidence with the medical evidence by P.W.27 goes to show that the occurrence was not seen by the witnesses as claimed and it did not happen in the manner as alleged by the prosecution. 

 43. The First Information Report and the charge sheet though not substantive evidence can be looked into for better appreciation of the prosecution case and from the charge sheet which is in the paper book it is found that the I.O. categorically stated that no valuables or articles were taken away by the dacoits. From the statement of the witnesses he found that it was a case of murder simplicitor and during his deposition before the Court as P.W.30, Shah Akil Uddin. O.C. admitted that সাক্ষী প্রমানে ডাকাতির আলামত পাই নাই।” Thus in absence of any evidence of dacoity by any of the witness and in absence of any recover of any article taken away during the dacoity from the possession of any of the accused person it can be safely said that the prosecution has hopelessly failed to prove the case of dacoity and therefore the charge under section 396 P.C. must fail on the ground of absence of eidetic to prove any of the ingredient of section 391 of the Penal Code. 

 44. Now coming to the confessional statement which is exhibit-10 quoted hereinbefore it will be clear that the same was extracted from accused Abdul Ali by severe torture, and intimidation. This finds support from his statement under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure wherein he stated that he was several beaten and he was in dying condition. It further finds support from the evidence of P.W. 29 Md. Mosharaf Hossain, Magistrate 1st Class who recorded dying declaration of accused Abdul Ali at 9-35 at night on the written requisition of Dr. M.A. Mannan at Sarail Upazilla Health Complex exhibit 24. From a reading of the deposition of P.W. 29 who recorded dying declaration it appears that the injuries of accused Abdul Ali were serious for which he gave a dying declaration on the day before the confessional statement by another Magistrate-cum T.N.O. was recorded. It is mysterious that although he was in the Thana Health Complex at 9-35 P.M. at night for recording dying declaration that is no discharge certificate from the Hospital and there is nothing on record that he was taken to police station and then to the Court on next day and under what condition. This depicts a picture that reflects high handedness of the investigating agency in this case. In such view of the matter exhibit 10, in our opinion, has been procured from its maker accused Abdul Ali condemned prisoner, by physical torture, threat and intimidation. This is pertinent to note that in the confessional statement he did not implicate himself with the murder of Paritosh rather he stated that it was Razzaque who gave the blow and he further stated that no valuables were taken away from the boat. 

 45. In view of our discussion as above we are constrains to hold that this is a case of no evidence and the prosecution has hopelessly failed to prove the charge under section 396 against any of the accused person beyond reasonable doubt and we are unable to maintain the impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge.
